author: Mark Atwood
text: Rust idiom confidence: ~85% chance of no missed idiom issue. Least confident flags: JMAP-ayoz.32 (the HashMap key allocation pattern is workspace-wide across all extension-server siblings — fixing it is a canonical-template question that affects 7 crates, not metadata-server alone; whether to fix at all vs document as deliberate-demo-grade-concession is a design judgment), JMAP-ayoz.33 (the 'as' cast pattern is also workspace-wide and the targets shipped are all 64-bit, so the lossy-truncation hazard is theoretical today; downgrading to opinion-tier if 32-bit support is explicitly not on the roadmap is reasonable). Uncertainty driven by: not having loaded the full canonical jmap-mail-server memory.rs (2742 lines) to verify every idiom convention used there — I cross-checked specific call sites (State::from, HashMap key shape, MemoryError struct shape) but did not exhaustively diff every function. Would raise confidence if: (a) a side audit of the canonical's memory.rs against this crate's memory.rs flagged or cleared every structural divergence beyond the 7 found, (b) the canonical's PLAN.md or AGENTS.md documented an explicit idiom-convention list (currently inferred from code-read), (c) the workspace had an idiomatic-rust check beyond clippy in CI (e.g. cargo-machete for unused deps, cargo-udeps for dead code) — cargo clippy --all-features came back clean on this crate, so the easy lints are covered.
